490:             if child.kind() != "catch_clause" {
491:                 Self::walk_catch_without_id(child, source, diagnostics);
492:             }

496:     /// RHSFN: Function name used on RHS without `@` handle prefix.
497:     ///
498:     /// Detects when a known MATLAB builtin function name is used as a variable
499:     /// (identifier) on the right-hand side of an assignment without `@`.
500:     fn check_rhs_function_name(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
501:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
502:         // Collect function definitions in this file.
503:         let defined_functions = collect_defined_functions(root, source);
504:         Self::walk_rhs_function_name(root, source, &defined_functions, &mut diagnostics);
505:         diagnostics
506:     }

508:     fn walk_rhs_function_name(
509:         node: Node,
510:         source: &str,
511:         defined_functions: &HashSet<String>,
512:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
513:     ) {
514:         if node.kind() == "assignment" {
515:             // Check the RHS for bare function name usage.
516:             if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2)) {
517:                 if rhs.kind() == "identifier" {
518:                     let name = node_text(rhs, source).trim();
519:                     // Only flag if the name matches a known defined function.
520:                     if defined_functions.contains(name) {
521:                         let pos = rhs.start_position();
522:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
523:                             rule_id: "RHSFN",
524:                             message: "The expression cannot be assigned to multiple values."
525:                                 .to_string(),
526:                             severity: Severity::Error,
527:                             byte_range: rhs.start_byte()..rhs.end_byte(),
528:                             line: pos.row + 1,
529:                             column: pos.column + 1,
530:                             fix: Some(Fix::new(
531:                                 rhs.start_byte()..rhs.end_byte(),
532:                                 format!("@{name}"),
533:                             )),
534:                         });
535:                     }
536:                 }
537:             }
538:         }
539: 
540:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
541:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
542:             Self::walk_rhs_function_name(child, source, defined_functions, diagnostics);
543:         }
544:     }

546:     /// VARARG: Misuse of varargin/varargout.
547:     ///
548:     /// Flags usage of `varargin` outside a function that declares it, or
549:     /// `varargout` in a function that doesn't have it as an output.
550:     fn check_vararg_misuse(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
551:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
552:         Self::walk_vararg_misuse(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
553:         diagnostics
554:     }

556:     fn walk_vararg_misuse(node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
557:         if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
558:             let func_text = node_text(node, source);
559:             let has_varargin_param = func_text.contains("varargin");
560:             let has_varargout_output = func_text.contains("varargout");
561: 
562:             // Check body for varargin/varargout usage.
563:             Self::check_vararg_in_body(
564:                 node,
565:                 source,
566:                 has_varargin_param,
567:                 has_varargout_output,
568:                 diagnostics,
569:             );
570:         }
571: 
572:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
573:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
574:             if child.kind() != "function_definition" {
575:                 Self::walk_vararg_misuse(child, source, diagnostics);
576:             }
577:         }
578:     }

580:     fn check_vararg_in_body(
581:         node: Node,
582:         source: &str,
583:         has_varargin: bool,
584:         has_varargout: bool,
585:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
586:     ) {
587:         if node.kind() == "identifier" {
588:             let name = node_text(node, source).trim();
589:             let misused =
590:                 (name == "varargin" && !has_varargin) || (name == "varargout" && !has_varargout);
591:             if misused {
592:                 let pos = node.start_position();
593:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
594:                     rule_id: "VARARG",
595:                     message: "Initialize VARARGOUT with a CELL.".to_string(),
596:                     severity: Severity::Error,
597:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
598:                     line: pos.row + 1,
599:                     column: pos.column + 1,
600:                     fix: None,
601:                 });
602:             }
603:         }
604: 
605:         // Don't recurse into nested function definitions.
606:         if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
607:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
608:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
609:                 if child.kind() != "function_definition" {
610:                     Self::check_vararg_in_body(
611:                         child,
612:                         source,
613:                         has_varargin,
614:                         has_varargout,
615:                         diagnostics,
616:                     );
617:                 }
618:             }
619:         } else {
620:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
621:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
622:                 Self::check_vararg_in_body(child, source, has_varargin, has_varargout, diagnostics);
623:             }
624:         }
625:     }

627:     /// Parfor-related checks: PFUIXE, PFBFN, PFWHOS, PFTUSE, PFRNC.
628:     fn check_parfor_issues(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
629:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
630:         Self::walk_parfor_issues(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
631:         diagnostics
632:     }
633: 
634:     fn walk_parfor_issues(node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
635:         if node.kind() == "for_statement" {
636:             let stmt_text = node_text(node, source);
637:             if !stmt_text.starts_with("parfor") {
638:                 // Not a parfor — recurse into children only.
639:                 let mut cursor = node.walk();
640:                 for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
641:                     Self::walk_parfor_issues(child, source, diagnostics);
642:                 }
643:                 return;
644:             }
645: 
646:             // This is a parfor. Extract the loop variable.
647:             let loop_var = extract_for_variable(node, source);
648: 
649:             // Walk the parfor body for issues.
650:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
651:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
652:                 if child.kind() == "block" {
653:                     Self::check_parfor_body(child, source, loop_var.as_deref(), diagnostics);
654:                 }
655:             }
656:         }
657: 
658:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
659:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
660:             Self::walk_parfor_issues(child, source, diagnostics);
661:         }
662:     }
663: 
664:     fn check_parfor_body(
665:         node: Node,
666:         source: &str,
667:         loop_var: Option<&str>,
668:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
669:     ) {
670:         match node.kind() {
671:             "function_call" => {
672:                 let func_name = extract_call_name(node, source);
673:                 if let Some(name) = &func_name {
674:                     // PFUIXE: Loop variable used in eval.
675:                     if *name == "eval" || *name == "evalin" || *name == "feval" {
676:                         if let Some(lv) = loop_var {
677:                             let args = collect_call_args(node, source);
678:                             if args.iter().any(|a| a.contains(lv)) {
679:                                 let pos = node.start_position();
680:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
681:                                     rule_id: "PFUIXE",
682:                                     message: format!(
683:                                         "The index variable {} might be used after the PARFOR loop on line {}, but it is unavailable after the loop.",
684:                                         lv, pos.row + 1
685:                                     ),
686:                                     severity: Severity::Error,
687:                                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
688:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
689:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
690:                                     fix: None,
691:                                 });
692:                             }
693:                         }
694:                     }
695: 
696:                     // PFWHOS: who/whos in parfor.
697:                     if *name == "who" || *name == "whos" {
698:                         let pos = node.start_position();
699:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
700:                             rule_id: "PFWHOS",
701:                             message: "Using \"who\" or \"whos\" without \"-file\" is invalid inside a PARFOR loop because it accesses the workspace in a non-transparent way.".to_string(),
702:                             severity: Severity::Error,
703:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
704:                             line: pos.row + 1,
705:                             column: pos.column + 1,
706:                             fix: None,
707:                         });
708:                     }
709: 
710:                     // PFBFN: Certain builtin functions problematic in parfor.
711:                     let problematic_builtins = [
712:                         "assignin",
713:                         "evalin",
714:                         "save",
715:                         "load",
716:                         "clear",
717:                         "global",
718:                         "persistent",
719:                     ];
720:                     if problematic_builtins.contains(name) {
721:                         let pos = node.start_position();
722:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
723:                             rule_id: "PFBFN",
724:                             message: "Use of this function is invalid inside a PARFOR loop because it accesses or modifies the workspace in a non-transparent way.".to_string(),
725:                             severity: Severity::Error,
726:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
727:                             line: pos.row + 1,
728:                             column: pos.column + 1,
729:                             fix: None,
730:                         });
731:                     }
732:                 }
733:             }
734:             "assignment" => {
735:                 // PFTUSE / PFRNC: Check for temporary variable misuse and
736:                 // inconsistent reduction patterns.
737:                 if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
738:                     if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
739:                         let var_name = node_text(lhs, source).trim().to_string();
740:                         if let Some(rhs) =
741:                             node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2))
742:                         {
743:                             let rhs_text = node_text(rhs, source);
744:                             // PFTUSE: Variable used on both sides but is not a reduction.
745:                             if rhs_text.contains(&var_name)
746:                                 && !is_reduction_pattern(&var_name, rhs, source)
747:                             {
748:                                 let pos = node.start_position();
749:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
750:                                     rule_id: "PFTUSE",
751:                                     message: format!(
752:                                         "The temporary variable {} is used after the PARFOR loop on line {}, but its value is not available after the loop.",
753:                                         var_name, pos.row + 1
754:                                     ),
755:                                     severity: Severity::Error,
756:                                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
757:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
758:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
759:                                     fix: None,
760:                                 });
761:                             }
762: 
763:                             // PFRNC: Reduction operator not consistent.
764:                             if is_reduction_pattern(&var_name, rhs, source) {
765:                                 // Check for mixed reduction operators on same variable.
766:                                 // This is a simplified check — full analysis would track
767:                                 // across the entire parfor body.
768:                                 if has_mixed_reduction_ops(&var_name, rhs, source) {
769:                                     let pos = node.start_position();
770:                                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
771:                                         rule_id: "PFRNC",
772:                                         message: format!(
773:                                             "Parfor reduction variable {} must be used in the same position in each assignment statement when using non-commutative reduction operations '*', '[,]', or '[;]'.",
774:                                             var_name
775:                                         ),
776:                                         severity: Severity::Error,
777:                                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
778:                                         line: pos.row + 1,
779:                                         column: pos.column + 1,
780:                                         fix: None,
781:                                     });
782:                                 }
783:                             }
784:                         }
785:                     }
786:                 }
787:             }
788:             _ => {}
789:         }
790: 
791:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
792:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
793:             Self::check_parfor_body(child, source, loop_var, diagnostics);
794:         }
795:     }
796: }

904: /// Find the condition child of an `if_statement` or `elseif_clause` node.
905: ///
906: /// In tree-sitter-matlab, the condition is typically the node between the
907: /// keyword (`if`/`elseif`/`while`) and the body.
908: pub(crate) fn find_condition_child(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
909:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
910:     let mut found_keyword = false;
911:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
912:         if child.kind() == "if"
913:             || child.kind() == "elseif"
914:             || child.kind() == "while"
915:             || child.is_named() && found_keyword
916:         {
917:             if found_keyword && child.kind() != "block" && child.kind() != "end" {
918:                 return Some(child);
919:             }
920:             if !child.is_named() || child.kind() == "if" || child.kind() == "while" {
921:                 found_keyword = true;
922:             }
923:         }
924:     }
925: 
926:     // Fallback: return the first named child that is not a keyword or block.
927:     let mut cursor2 = node.walk();
928:     let result = node.children(&mut cursor2).find(|child| {
929:         child.is_named()
930:             && child.kind() != "block"
931:             && child.kind() != "elseif_clause"
932:             && child.kind() != "else_clause"
933:             && child.kind() != "end"
934:             && child.kind() != "comment"
935:     });
936:     result
937: }

943:         .children(&mut cursor)

969: /// Extract the function name from a `function_call` node.
970: pub(crate) fn extract_call_name<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
971:     if node.kind() != "function_call" {
972:         return None;
973:     }
974: 
975:     // Try the `name` field first.
976:     if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
977:         if name_node.kind() == "identifier" {
978:             return Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()]);
979:         }
980:         // For field_expression (e.g., obj.method), return the full text.
981:         return Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()]);
982:     }
983: 
984:     // Fallback: first identifier child.
985:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
986:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
987:         if child.kind() == "identifier" {
988:             return Some(&source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()]);
989:         }
990:     }
991: 
992:     None
993: }

995: /// Collect arguments from a `function_call` node as text strings.

1002:             for arg in child.children(&mut arg_cursor) {
1003:                 if arg.is_named() {

1005:                 }

1007:             return args;
1008:         }
1009:     }

1019: /// Find the operator text in a binary/boolean/comparison operator node.
1020: pub(crate) fn find_operator_text<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> String {
1021:     // The operator is typically the second child (index 1), which is an
1022:     // anonymous node containing the operator symbol.
1023:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1024:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1025:         if !child.is_named() {
1026:             let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
1027:             let trimmed = text.trim();
1028:             if !trimmed.is_empty() && trimmed != "(" && trimmed != ")" && trimmed != "," {
1029:                 return trimmed.to_string();
1030:             }
1031:         }
1032:     }
1033: 
1034:     // Fallback: try the operator field.
1035:     if let Some(op_node) = node.child_by_field_name("operator") {
1036:         return node_text(op_node, source).trim().to_string();
1037:     }
1038: 
1039:     // Last resort: parse from the full text.
1040:     let text = node_text(node, source);
1041:     for op in &[
1042:         "&&", "||", "==", "~=", ">=", "<=", ">", "<", ".+", ".-", ".*", "./", ".\\", ".^", "+",
1043:         "-", "*", "/", "\\", "^", "&", "|",
1044:     ] {
1045:         if text.contains(op) {
1046:             return (*op).to_string();
1047:         }
1048:     }
1049: 
1050:     String::new()
1051: }

1053: /// Check if a node is inside a loop (`for_statement` or `while_statement`).
1054: pub(crate) fn is_inside_loop(node: Node) -> bool {
1055:     let mut current = node.parent();
1056:     while let Some(parent) = current {
1057:         if parent.kind() == "for_statement" || parent.kind() == "while_statement" {
1058:             return true;
1059:         }
1060:         current = parent.parent();
1061:     }
1062:     false

1065: /// Check if a node is in a boolean context (condition of if/while/elseif).
1066: pub(crate) fn is_in_boolean_context(node: Node) -> bool {
1067:     let mut current = node.parent();
1068:     while let Some(parent) = current {
1069:         match parent.kind() {
1070:             "if_statement" | "while_statement" | "elseif_clause" => {
1071:                 // Check if the node is in the condition part, not the body.
1072:                 // The condition comes before the first block child.
1073:                 let in_condition = true;
1074:                 let mut cursor = parent.walk();
1075:                 for child in parent.children(&mut cursor) {
1076:                     if child.kind() == "block" {
1077:                         break;

12: /// Parse MATLAB source and return the tree.

14:     let mut parser = Parser::new();

27:     }

31: /// the Linter's depth-first dispatch. Returns all diagnostics.
32: pub fn lint_nodes(rule: &dyn Rule, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
33:     let tree = parse(source);
34:     let path = std::path::Path::new("test.m");
35:     let targets: Vec<&str> = rule.target_node_types().to_vec();
36:     let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();

40:         source: &str,
41:         path: &std::path::Path,

45:     ) {
46:         if targets.contains(&node.kind()) {
47:             let ctx = NodeContext {
48:                 node,
49:                 source,
50:                 file_path: path,
51:             };

53:         }
